newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Esselte says profits may rise 10 pct '97.
newsitem.headline: Esselte says profits may rise 10 pct '97.

text.p: Swedish office supplier Esselte said on Thursday there was still a good chance that pre-tax profit would rise by 10 percent in 1997.
Esselte posted a two percent rise in pre-tax profits to 194 million crowns ($25.1 million) for the first three months of the year when sales rose to 3.15 billion crowns fron 3.02 billion a year ago.
"The forecast given in the 1996 annual report, that Esselte has good possibilities to reach its target of a 10 percent increase in pre-tax income in 1997, remains valid," Esselte said in a statement.
Esselte said acquired units accounted for most of the rise in sales in the first quarter.
The depreciation in the crown added 80 million crowns to sales in that period while profits decreased by five million crowns as a result of foreign currency translations.
Sales in the office products area rose seven percent.
"The trend of sales has been very strong in North America but was weak in Central and Northern Europe, Japan and Australia," the statement said.
Sales of labelling systems increased in France but were weak in Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden while sales of hand-held price marking tools continued to fall.
Esselte said sales of electronic article surveillance systems were strong and sales in the picture framing area were on the same level as the first quarter of 1996.
Esselte shares were trading 3.5 crowns higher at 182 crowns at 1300 GMT.
